cancel_execution.description: Stop a run that is still going. Use it to cut a query loose that is taking longer than it is worth: a cancelled run stops consuming compute, though the credits already spent on it stay spent. Only a run still in flight can be cancelled: Dune has nothing to stop once one has finished, and answers that it cannot find the run at all, so check the status first if the run might already be over.

run_query.description: Run a query saved on Dune and get its rows back in one step. Running a query on Dune is normally three calls (start it, watch it, collect it), and this does all three: it submits the run, waits for it to finish, and returns the rows, the columns and what it cost in credits. Give it the query's address from dune.com, fill in any parameters the query takes, and narrow the result with the row, column, filter and ordering options so you only pay for the data you actually use. If the query is still running when the wait runs out, the step still succeeds and hands back the execution id for a later step to collect.

parameters.description: The query to run, as its id or its address on dune.com. Open the query on Dune and either copy the whole address from the browser bar or take the number out of it: https://dune.com/queries/1215383 and 1215383 both work.

run_sql.description: Write DuneSQL and get the answer back, without saving a query first. Dune's warehouse holds decoded data for 100+ chains (blocks, transactions, logs, token transfers, prices, NFT trades and the community's curated tables on top of them), and this runs a statement straight against it, waits for it, and returns the rows. Use Search tables first if you don't know what a table is called. Note that Dune charges for the compute a statement uses, so filter by time and select only the columns you need.

mock_response.sql: select block_date, project, sum(amount_usd) as volume_usd from dex.trades group by 1, 2

run_sql.name: run_sql

parameters.description: The DuneSQL to run. Dune's SQL is Trino-flavoured: single quotes for text, double quotes for column names that need them, and interval arithmetic for dates.

examples.label: Yesterday's DEX volume by project
examples.value:
select project, sum(amount_usd) as volume_usd
from dex.trades
where block_time > now() - interval '1' day
group by 1
order by 2 desc
limit 20

examples.label: A wallet's recent transactions
examples.value:
select block_time, hash, value / 1e18 as eth
from ethereum.transactions
where "from" = 0xd8da6bf26964af9d7eed9e03e53415d37aa96045
  and block_time > now() - interval '7' day
order by block_time desc

upsert_materialized_view.description: Store a query's results as a table that refreshes on a schedule. Anything reading the view gets an answer instantly and for far fewer credits than re-running the query, which is what makes an expensive query usable in a dashboard or on an hourly workflow. Pick how often it should refresh (Dune allows anything from every 15 minutes to weekly), and Dune keeps it current on its own. Naming a view that already exists updates it; either way a refresh starts straight away.
